extracted.intended_audience: The people of New York; voters and citizens considering the proposed Constitution; legislators and engaged public
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and arguments for what constitutes a good national Executive under a constitution—balancing 'energy' (effectiveness) with republican 'safety' (dependence on the people and responsibility). The text analyzes election method, tenure, powers, checks, and institutional form (single magistrate vs plurality/council).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electors must be independent of federal officeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: No senator, representative, or other person holding a place of trust or profit under the United States, can be of the numbers of the electors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: excluding current federal officeholders ensures the immediate agents in the election are 'free from any sinister bias.' Their transient existence and detached situation reduce risk of corruption because bribing or coordinating a dispersed body across many states would require time and means. Anti-pattern: allowing federal officeholders to serve as electors risks capture or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral process: state-chosen electors, majority rule, House contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: The people of each State shall choose a number of persons as electors, equal to the number of senators and representatives of such State, who shall assemble within the State, and vote for some fit person as President; the person who has a majority of the whole number of votes will be the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no candidate has a majority, the House of Representatives shall select from the five highest vote-getters the man best qualified. This design aims to produce a President who commands support across the Union rather than only statewide popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electors should be transient and detached agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Their transient existence, and their detached situation... afford a satisfactory prospect of their continuing so, to the conclusion of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transient, detached electors are less likely to be engaged in long-term corrupting bargains; dispersed electors across states make sudden collusion difficult. This is presented as a safeguard against combined motives that could mislead electors from duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive independence in tenure (continuance dependent only on the people)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive should be independent for his continuance in office on all but the people themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: independence prevents the Executive from sacrificing duty to complaisance for those whose favor is necessary to his duration in office. The system secures this by making re-election depend on a special body deputed for that purpose. Anti-pattern: dependence on other political actors undermines impartial administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy in the Executive (necessary public-good function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy in the Executive is a leading character in the definition of good government. It is essential to the protection of the community against foreign attacks... steady administration of the laws; protection of property... security of liberty against ambition, faction, and anarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hamilton lists energy as a primary goal and motivates institutional choices (unity, duration, support, competent powers) as ingredients creating executive energy. Weak execution = bad government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredients of executive energy: unity, duration, support, competent powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The ingredients which constitute energy in the Executive are, first, unity; secondly, duration; thirdly, an adequate provision for its support; fourthly, competent powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ingredient is necessary to produce a vigorous executive able to act decisively in crises and to administer the laws effectively. The text then analyzes how each contributes and how they can be balanced with safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety in a republican executive: due dependence on the people and due responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The ingredients which constitute safety in the republican sense are, first, a due dependence on the people, secondly, a due responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are counterweights to executive energy: dependence ensures accountability to the electorate; responsibility ensures censure and punishment for misconduct (especially in elective offices). Institutional features (impeachment, re-election mechanisms) serve these ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity: preference for a single executive magistrate
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision, activity, secrecy, and despatch will generally characterize the proceedings of one man in a much more eminent degree than the proceedings of any greater number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity favors prompt and decisive action—important in war and emergency. Dangers of plurality: dissension, weakened authority, distracted plans, factional splits, and loss of responsibility. Anti-pattern: plurality of equal magistrates or an executive council that is constitutionally necessary produces delay, feebleness, and concealed faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality/council undermines responsibility and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The plurality of the Executive tends to deprive the people of the two greatest securities... first, the restraints of public opinion... and, secondly, the opportunity of discovering with facility and clearness the misconduct... Responsibility is of two kinds: to censure and to punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple actors allow shifting blame ('I was overruled by my council'), make it hard to detect culpability, encourage collusion, and reduce the efficacy of public censure. Examples: state councils that produce scandalous appointments where blame is shifted between governor and council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of office should balance fidelity and avoidance of permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: That magistrate is to be elected for FOUR years; and is to be re-eligible as often as the people... shall think him worthy of their confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration contributes to energy (stability, continuity) but limited term and re-eligibility prevent hereditary permanence and allow accountability. Comparison used: four years for federal chief magistrate vs three years for a state governor; longer terms in single states may more easily establish dangerous influence than a similar federal term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate provision for support to secure independence
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequate provision for its support [is an ingredient of energy].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial and institutional support prevents dependence on other actors or factions; this autonomy enables decisive action and reduces inducements to corrupt bargains. (The text identifies support as necessary but focuses more on the principle than concrete mechanisms here.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent powers: enumerated executive authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is to be the 'commander-in-chief'... to grant reprieves and pardons... to recommend to the consideration of Congress measures... to convene both houses... to take care that the laws be faithfully executed; and to commission all officers of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent powers give the executive real capacity to act. The text distinguishes substantive scope (e.g., commander-in-chief but not the power to declare war or raise armies) and observes that some powers are concurrent with or checked by other branches (treaties require Senate two-thirds, appointments require Senate advice and consent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited military authority: commander-in-chief with legislative war powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is to be commander-in-chief of the army and navy... but the declaring of war and the raising and regulating of fleets and armies would appertain to the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation intentionally confines the President's military role to direction and command of forces while leaving war declaration and force-raising to the legislature—reducing risk of unilateral military adventurism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified veto rather than absolute negative
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is to have power to return a bill... the bill so returned is to become a law, if... it be approved by two thirds of both houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A qualified veto (return for reconsideration with a legislative override) differs fundamentally from an absolute royal negative; it balances executive check with legislative primacy and provides a moderate restraining power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments and treaties should involve legislative concurrence to limit patronage
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is to nominate, and, with the advice and consent of the Senate, to appoint ambassadors... judges of the Supreme Court, and in general all officers of the United States established by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring Senate concurrence creates publicity and a larger body harder to influence than small state councils, thereby reducing corruption and private patronage. The treaty power requires two-thirds of Senators present, tempering executive autonomy in foreign policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pardoning power limited by impeachment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to have power to grant reprieves and pardons for offenses against the United States, EXCEPT IN CASES OF IMPEACHMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation prevents the Executive from using pardons to shield political wrongdoing that could be addressed by impeachment, preserving a route to political accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reception of ambassadors as dignity, not substantive authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is also to be authorized to receive ambassadors and other public ministers. This... is more a matter of dignity than of authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical convenience (no need to convene legislature on every diplomatic arrival) justifies vesting this formality in the Executive while not implying it grants substantive unilateral foreign powers.
